result.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models
result.summary: Can changing which matrices receive 2, 4, or 8 bits improve a small language model without increasing its parameter storage? I compare two parent-selection rules in the same genetic algorithm: a binary-tournament variant and an Alternis-inspired rule. A separate baseline samples repaired random allocations without crossover or mutation. All three use the same MLX affine quantizer, byte ceiling, initialization and candidate allowance within each study. An exploratory study on Qwen3.5-2B evaluates 90 allocations per run. The main study on Qwen3-1.7B evaluates 500 distinct allocations per run over 10 paired seeds. Against uniform four-bit, tournament reduces held-out next-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) by 0.0616 on AG News and 0.0152 on IMDb on average, improving all 10 seeds on each corpus at identical parameter storage. Alternis improves five seeds and ties five on AG News; on IMDb its mean gain is near zero. Random returns uniform four-bit in every seed. The tournament representative answers 156 of 400 ARC-Challenge questions correctly versus 163 for uniform; no accuracy gain is demonstrated on this subset. The result favors this tournament variant for text prediction under the tested protocol, not for compression ratio or task accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在相同遗传算法框架下比较两种父代选择规则与一个无交叉变异的随机基线，在固定参数字节上限下为小型语言模型各矩阵分配 2/4/8 bit 量化精度，并以 Qwen3-1.7B 上的 held-out 下一词 NLL 为主要评价指标，结论是 tournament 规则优于均匀 4-bit，但未在 ARC-Challenge 上体现精度收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定存储预算下逐模块精度分配 + 留出集选优」的搜索与选择流程，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态、缓存或子模块的容量/精度分配及候选筛选提供类比线索，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态，需较多核查。
